sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling from the finite multinomial observed law \(P\).
sampling_model.units: The observations are \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), with fixed finite \(\mathcal X\), binary treatment, and \(K\)-category outcomes.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is observational; a candidate full law uses \(q_{xij}=Q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y(0)=i,Y(1)=j)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The observed propensity satisfies \(\varepsilon\leq e_x\leq1-\varepsilon\) on positive-mass strata.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All nuisance quantities are multinomial cell probabilities. Simultaneous cell-frequency concentration and the dual Lipschitz modulus deliver the finite-sample regular-region band; the open local theory uses an estimated directional derivative under weaker facial regularity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The average-case sensitivity model leads to sharp bounds for \(E[Y(0)]\) and \(E[Y(1)]\), respectively.
The estimated range converges to the narrowest possible interval that must contain the true treatment effect.
Equations (10), (12), and (14) replace the base-policy \(f\)-divergence constraint by its Jensen lower bound and conditional moment constraints on observed-data weights.
Monotone treatment response is maintained as a substantive restriction on individual response behavior.
The paper derives a Hadamard directional derivative for finite-valued Slater-regular linear SOCP optimal values.
An alternative resampling scheme is proposed which remains consistent when the bootstrap fails.
The paper develops uniform derivative-bootstrap inference for finite-valued function-valued optimization maps.

body.tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. An explicit embedding into the published Ishikawa--He--Kanamori Neyman-divergence Jensen--CMC program proves the same-budget separation \(9/70>9/91\). On a named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, profile bands have finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) diameter, while a contiguous boundary pair proves that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.

project_justification.gap: Average-case sensitivity analysis has sharp armwise potential-outcome bounds but no jointly attained ATE frontier. Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's published \(f\)-divergence computation uses Jensen and conditional-moment relaxations whose cross-world realizability is unresolved. Existing inference theory does not quantify both the regular finite-sample width and the finite-to-infinite boundary obstruction for this frontier.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes make the missing joint law explicit and expose a response-type garbling geometry that is invisible to armwise reweighting.
project_justification.fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, embeds the full-law model into the published Jensen--CMC program with identical budget normalization, and pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem with a contiguous boundary lower bound.

body.related_work: Zhang and Zhao motivate average rather than worst-case assignment distortion and prove sharp bounds for each average potential outcome, but their discussion explicitly withholds joint ATE attainment. Dorn and Guo prove simultaneous ATE sharpness for the worst-case odds model through a two-point extremal construction; their compatible-law logic informs the present proof, while the shared strictly convex budget changes the optimizer. Ishikawa, He, and Kanamori define an observed-policy-first \(f\)-divergence in their equation (10), apply Jensen in equation (12), and combine the relaxed divergence with CMC in equation (14). Theorem 6 uses \(f_N(r)=r^{-1}-1\), proves that their unrelaxed budget equals \(R_P\), maps each compatible full law into their weight set, and gives the strict same-budget ATE-slice separation \(9/70>9/91\). Balke and Pearl supply the finite response-type representation, and Manski supplies the substantive monotone-response benchmark; Theorem 3 differs by deriving monotone support for an extremal law without assuming it of the population. Duan, Zhang, and Zhang derive directional derivatives for finite-valued Slater-regular SOCP values, while Fang and Santos and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker supply derivative-aware statistical inference. Theorems 7 and 8 establish regular finite-sample diameter control and a nonregular boundary lower bound; the weaker facial conditions and adaptive derivative bootstrap remain Open-ended Question 1.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The interior binary stationarity equation is generically quintic, so the exact catalog isolates a unique algebraic root and does not promise universal radical formulas. The finite regular-profile constant can deteriorate as the observed-cell or Slater margin \(\delta\) approaches zero; Theorem 8 shows that this deterioration reflects a genuine statistical discontinuity at the null-feasibility boundary.
body.honest_scope: The sharpness, dual attainment, garbling, scalar catalog, explicit published-program embedding, strict relaxation gap, regular-region finite-sample diameter, and boundary impossibility are theorem claims to be proved. Uniform tangent inference under weaker facial regularity and adaptive derivative-bootstrap inversion remain open. The \(\Gamma=1\) specialization is retained only as a regression corollary. The application target is a prespecified categorical mercury score and finite covariate stratification; it does not claim to recover the original continuous-outcome NHANES estimand.
